item.title: Europe Cannot Avoid an AI Reckoning
item.description: Given the risks it faces from all sides, Europe must move past its focus on regulatory excellence. Unless it makes rapid strides toward building the physical and financial infrastructure that a domestic European AI industry will need, such preoccupations will prove to be more of a liability than an asset.

item.title: Trump’s Failure of the Will
item.description: Donald Trump’s shock-and-awe approach to politics has often been compared to authoritarian and fascist leaders who have consolidated power through grand political spectacles. But these accounts conflate shock with genuine spectacle, which Trump is incapable of producing.

item.title: Trump’s Iran Gamble
item.description: Although it is still possible that US President Donald Trump could accept a limited nuclear deal with Iran that allows him to declare victory, the more likely scenario is that he will try to repeat his recent success in Venezuela. There is just one problem: Iran is not Venezuela.

item.title: The Financial Gulf Stream Is Nearing a Tipping Point
item.description: For decades, the global economy rested on a financial arrangement that allowed the United States to borrow cheaply and absorb much of the world’s surplus output. But that system is beginning to come undone amid escalating geopolitical tensions and growing doubts about US policy stability.

item.title: Trump Is Destroying the Far-Right Brand
item.description: With its unparalleled global visibility, the United States offers an unavoidable case study of radical right-wing governance in action. Just as Brexit ultimately strengthened support for the European Union, MAGA-era America may serve as a cautionary example, weakening the appeal of authoritarianism in other democracies.

item.title: Democracy Dies in Broad Daylight
item.description: In America today, journalism still exists, but the chain that once ran from reporting to shared reality to institutional response has begun to break apart. The consequence is a democracy where truth no longer matters, because facts can be published, verified, and still fail to trigger a response.

item.title: Will Democracy Govern Capitalism - or Be Consumed by It?
item.description: Following aggressive lobbying by the Trump administration, more than 145 countries agreed to give big US multinationals a free pass under the global corporate minimum tax rules that were agreed in 2021. But if democracy is to prevail over oligarchy, policymakers must tax extreme wealth appropriately – and they must do it fast.

item.title: Europe Should Reject US-Style Competitiveness
item.description: European leaders seem increasingly convinced that, to succeed in the 21st century, they must reshape Europe's economy in America’s image. But the American brand of "competitiveness" contributes to major imbalances and far-reaching harm, which the European Union can avoid by embracing effective competition policy.

item.title: Kevin Warsh’s Dangerous Monetary Nostalgia
item.description: The next US Federal Reserve chair seems to think that the large size of the central bank’s balance sheet reflects a discretionary policy choice which can and should be reversed. In reality, however, the Fed's balance sheet has become part of the financial system’s core infrastructure, and shrinking it would carry serious risks.

item.title: A Path to Universal Prosperity by 2100
item.description: Over the past century, economic growth has delivered higher incomes and longer lives, while empowering millions of people. Looking to the future, a world where everyone can live securely and with options – as opposed to just subsisting – is within reach, but will require emerging economies to continue expanding.
